task:
# T04 — Ambiguity probe

Make the task list less cluttered by hiding completed tasks when appropriate.

spec.goal: Reduce clutter in the task list by conditionally hiding completed tasks, while preserving the existing task-list API unless the product rule says otherwise.
requirements: The app currently exposes GET /tasks with an optional status query parameter: status=pending returns pending tasks, status=completed returns completed tasks, and an omitted status returns all tasks.
The app currently represents completion with status="completed" and reopening with status="pending"; completedAt is populated/cleared accordingly.
The requested change concerns task-list visibility; no change to task creation, completion, reopening, task representation, or single-task retrieval is specified.
constraints: Only status values pending and completed are currently accepted by GET /tasks; other values return 400 with error invalid_status.
The implementation should remain consistent with the existing TypeScript task service and route structure.
No repository evidence defines what “when appropriate” means or establishes a UI-specific preference/settings mechanism.
nonGoals: Do not change task lifecycle transitions or completedAt behavior.
Do not change task object fields or GET /tasks/:id behavior.
Do not invent a persistence layer, user preference, authentication rule, or time-based archival policy.
acceptance: Pending human decision on the rule that determines when completed tasks are hidden.
Once the rule is decided, acceptance should verify the corresponding GET /tasks response for mixed pending/completed data, explicit status filters, and the empty/completed-only cases as applicable.
Existing behavior for task creation, completion, reopening, invalid status values, and single-task lookup should remain passing unless the decided rule explicitly changes one of them.
verification: Add or update focused route/service tests for the decided default visibility rule and any newly specified opt-in/opt-out control.
Run the existing test suite and verify status filtering and lifecycle tests remain green.
Verify that completed tasks are not deleted and remain retrievable through any explicitly supported completed-task view.

ambiguities.question: What exactly does “when appropriate” mean: should GET /tasks with no status parameter hide completed tasks by default, or should hiding require an explicit query parameter, user preference, or another condition?
ambiguities.basis: The raw task only says to hide completed tasks “when appropriate.” Existing code has no preference/settings concept and currently returns all tasks when status is omitted, but existing behavior cannot authorize a new product default.

ambiguities.question: If completed tasks are hidden by default, how should a caller request/show completed tasks?
ambiguities.basis: The repository already supports status=completed and status=pending, so preserving status=completed is plausible, but the task does not explicitly say whether that existing filter is the intended way to reveal hidden tasks or whether a new visibility parameter is required.

ambiguities.question: Should the existing behavior of GET /tasks without status (currently returning both pending and completed tasks) change, and should explicit status=pending or status=completed semantics change?
ambiguities.basis: Changing omitted-status behavior is externally observable. Existing tests document current behavior, but tests are not authority for the intended new behavior absent a precise rule; the task does not specify the treatment of explicit filters.
